channel.description:
Nature Communications is an open access, multidisciplinary journal dedicated to publishing high-quality research in all areas of the biological, health, physical, chemical and Earth sciences. Papers published by the journal aim to represent important advances of significance to specialists within each field.

We are committed to providing an efficient service for both authors and readers. Our team of independent editors make rapid and fair publication decisions. Prompt dissemination of accepted papers to a wide readership and beyond is achieved through a programme of continuous online publication.

item.title: [7] Twisted superconducting quantum diodes for high fidelity anharmonic qubits
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Igor Žutić, Yingying Wu

Authors: Han Zhong, Denis Kochan, Igor Žutić, Yingying Wu

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Study of twisted NbSe2 superconducting properties with relevance to van der Waals systems.

Tags: #superconductivity #NbSe2 #twisted

Abstract: Superconducting diodes can provide nonreciprocal elements for superconducting and quantum circuits, but the role of diode efficiency in quantum-device performance remains unclear. Here, the authors demonstrate an enhanced superconducting diode effect in twisted NbSe2 and show that even a moderate degree of nonreciprocity is sufficient to stabilize anharmonic qubit circuits.
